M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a red steel crowbar, about 32 long), the outline reads as a crowbar in every side view: one long straight shaft with a bent hook at one end (sides.png, top and below views) and a plain grey end at the other. The outline matches the brief with no part sticking out or missing.

M2.reason: Measured length is 31.2 against the brief's 32, a 2.6% difference. Width 1.1 and height 6.8 are not given a target by the brief, and the length is well inside 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, listed down to the small ones: a shaft (present, red), a claw at one end (only a bent tube end, with no flattened hook or fork, visible in in-hand.png and the BELOW view), a worn steel tip at each end (present, grey, in sides.png and in-hand.png). The claw is the missing or misshapen part, so M3 is held to 1.

M4.reason: The shaft is red painted metal and the tips are bare grey steel, as the brief asks ('red-painted steel', 'worn to bare metal at the tips'). Both regions have the right colour and material in sides.png, in-hand.png and attack.png.

M5.reason: The wear the brief asks for is there at both tips: the grey bare metal sits at the claw end and the far end in sides.png, attack.png (frames 9 and 10) and in-hand.png. The red paint has a soft gradient and no grain, but the brief names no other markings.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, which is measured apart. In the line-up (lineup.png), judges picked D, A, B where the asset was D, B, C. It passed for one of the game's, so the cap is held at 2.

M7.reason: The brief sets no front, and nothing in the views shows the weapon facing the wrong way. The shaft is upright and the claw end points the expected way in first-person.png and in-hand.png, so no fault is visible.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty, so SMAK's GoldSrc check passes. There are 56 triangles, far below twice Half-Life's median of 142. The ends are closed in every side view (sides.png, BELOW and TOP), and no part is open or floating.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset's rod sits left of centre and runs off the top and bottom of the frame, while the game's own crowbar sits right with its claw up at top right. The claw, which would sit at the top if the grip matched, is not in the asset's frame, so it does not sit where the original does. The hands are not drawn in attack.png, so I cannot judge a part from the hands there, and I do not charge it for leaving them.
